triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All nine rules ended at 2026-02-14, a placeholder the pre-fix summary admitted was 'a conservative no-later-than bound', so the module kept applying the terminated heading's +15% Liechtenstein duty for three months after Annex II terminated heading 9903.02.36 for goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. November 14, 2025.
triage.triage_notes: Read the source: resolve_provision.py on us/rulemaking/federal-register/2025-12-18/2025-23316 confirms 'Annex II Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on November 14, 2025 ... 1. Headings 9903.02.36 and 9903.02.58 are hereby terminated.' effective_to 2025-11-13 is the correct inclusive last day. Diff changes only effective_to (9x), the module summary, module source_verification (single corpus_citation_path -> corpus_citation_paths with the FR notice added), and adds one effective_period proof atom per rule; no formula, rate, input or scope change.
triage.verifier_justification: The only meaning-bearing change is the version window: all nine rules move `versions[0].effective_to` from '2026-02-14' to '2025-11-13' while every formula, input, output, and `effective_from` is untouched. Reading the sources through the pinned release settles that the pre-fix window disagreed with the law: the HTS text for 9903.02.36 carries only "[Compiler's note: provision terminated. See 90 Fed. Reg. 59281.]" with no date, and that notice's Annex II states the modifications are "effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on November 14, 2025" and that "Headings 9903.02.36 and 9903.02.58 are hereby terminated." The pre-fix encoding thus kept the terminated heading's +15% duty live three months past termination, so this is a source disagreement, not added precision, and not mechanical (dates changed, not only excerpts or citation strings). The competing kind untraceable_branch (a placeholder value with no source basis) is subsumed by the more specific effective-date kind, since nothing but the period bound moved.
triage.verifier_notes: Verified end to end, read-only. Diff bundle: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/4d2856a958/002.diff. git diff --stat vs parent 75a3677870: 58 insertions, 11 deletions, one file; the 11 deletions are the summary line plus the single old corpus_citation_path plus the nine old effective_to lines, so no formula, input, output, or scope changed. Refutations tried and rejected: (1) mechanical fails because effective_to is a version-window value, not an excerpt or citation string; the provenance edits (corpus_citation_paths, nine new effective_period proof atoms, summary rewrite) ride along with a real date change. (2) not_a_defect ("new source, old bound was a documented placeholder") fails because the module positively asserted a window through 2026-02-14 that the cited HTS note's own referenced notice contradicts; the pre-fix summary even admits the bound was invented ("a conservative no-later-than bound, the last day before the successor floor headings' 2026-02-15 panel domain"). (3) reclassify to untraceable_branch is defensible in the abstract but loses to the more specific date/version-window kind. (4) boundary_direction fails: the inclusive-end convention ("effective_to 2025-11-13 is the last effective day (inclusive end)") is a representation choice, not the defect; the defect is the three-month overrun. Source confirmation used resolve_provision.py at --rulespec-commit 4d2856a958, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provisions file line 1196 (HTS 9903.02.36) and line 12 (FR 2025-12-18/2025-23316); the Annex II excerpt in the new proof atoms matches the corpus text modulo the FR hard-wrap normalization the commit message discloses. Materiality note for a reviewer: the successor headings 9903.02.87/.88 (also in this commit) use the 15%-floor mechanic rather than a flat +15% additive, so the corrected handoff changes computed duty, not just labels.
